document: ET-8b — why gen1's decision-2/3 heads came back at chance, and it is not the accumulation limb failing
finding: gen1's heads were fitted on gen0's OWN trajectories on tasks < 226 — the tasks gen0's head had memorised. On those tasks gen0 finds the true bug region at decision 1 in 100% of episodes. gen1 was therefore trained on a situation that occurs 100% of the time in its training data and 22.4% of the time in its held-out evaluation.
the_error_in_one_line: Withdrawing +35.0 fixed how gen0 was REPORTED. It did not fix gen0's episodes as DATA, and they were used as gen1's training input.

gen1_heads_as_fitted.note: see et8b_gen1_heads.json for the full table and controls; d1 40.0% is IDENTICAL to gen0's d1 and correctly so — at decision 1 nothing has happened yet, so the state cannot differ between arms. A generation can only differ from decision 2 onward.

mean_abs_weight.reading: an order of magnitude smaller — the optimiser found nothing to fit

CONTROL_is_it_the_row_count.question: gen1 has fewer training rows than gen0 (638 vs 1014 at d2). Is that the explanation?
CONTROL_is_it_the_row_count.method: refit gen0's states at gen1's exact row count, 3 random draws
CONTROL_is_it_the_row_count.verdict: NO — gen0's states at gen1's row count are still 54-56%, nowhere near chance.

CONTROL_is_it_the_task_residue.question: gen0 solves more episodes early, so the tasks still alive at decision 2 are a harder residue. Is THAT the explanation?
CONTROL_is_it_the_task_residue.method: restrict gen0's states to the SAME task ids that reach that decision in gen1, and refit
CONTROL_is_it_the_task_residue.verdict: NO — same tasks, same row counts, same extractor, same layer. The difference is what the states ARE.

THE_CAUSE_measured.statistic: fraction of episodes in which the TRUE bug region had already been hypothesized before decision k
THE_CAUSE_measured.reading: On the 225 tasks its head memorised, gen0 finds the true region at decision 1 in EVERY episode. Those are exactly the trajectories gen1's d2/d3 heads were fitted on. Chance-level held-out accuracy is the expected consequence of a training distribution that is not a sample of the test distribution — it is not evidence that there is nothing to accumulate on.

THE_FIX.design: 3-fold cross-fitting over tasks 1-225: fold f is run by a head fitted on the other two folds only, so no episode is steered by a head that saw its task. 225 gen0-steered trajectories, none memorised. Tasks 226-300 are touched by nothing in it.
THE_FIX.gate: the chain re-reads train_ranges out of each npz and refuses to launch a fold whose head overlaps it — the first version of this rule was a sentence in a commit message, and a sentence is what failed
THE_FIX.verification: the chain re-prints the statistic above for the cross-fitted runs; the cross-fitted row must look like the BASE row, not like the contaminated one

scope: 8a is unaffected: it evaluated on slice 4 with a head fitted on 1-225 and never ran a second generation. This defect is confined to the loop chain, which is 8b.
gen0's HELD-OUT result (+17.3 [5.3, 29.3], McNemar p=0.0146) stands — it is measured on tasks 226-300, which no head in the chain has seen.
The gen1 arm run against these heads is reported as what it is: a head trained on a distribution it is not tested on. It is not a measurement of accumulation.
